In the later historical out-of-sample period, the strategy earns 5.4 cents per unit ($t=3.9$) on MLB spreads and 5.0 cents per unit ($t=5.1$) on MLB totals. Both remain below their development levels. NFL spreads earn 2.6 cents per unit ($t=1.2$), while totals earn 0.1 cents per unit ($t=0.1$). 

The NFL figures use the five-second decision interval adopted after the first evaluation. Under the original 60-second grid, spreads earn -2.0 cents per unit ($t=-0.5$) and totals 1.8 cents per unit ($t=0.5$). The comparison therefore remains subject to the protocol-change qualification in Chapter~\ref{ch:data}.
